newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on futures, premiums stagnant.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on futures, premiums stagnant.

text.p: NWE gas oil fell on Tuesday, although premiums stagnated, as a hefty drop in benchmark IPE futures pressured outright prices, traders said.
June IPE gas oil settled $5.75 lower at $172.00 a tonne as the market was dragged lower by losses on NYMEX.
Traders said the market had been quieter than expected following Britain's public holiday on Monday.
"I think a lot of people had a feeling prices might come off today," said one trader. "Even so activity's not really picked up much even with the fall in futures."
A number of buyers expected better demand on Wednesday.
Heating oil barges traded at June IPE $1.25 and $1.50 a tonne fob ARA, while 6,000 tonnes of Swiss spec material was heard done at $2.0 in the morning.
Traders said the cargo was looking under pressure with of Russian material on offer. A refiner was heard offering two May cargoes and a trader held three early June cargoes.
Premiums on such material were assessed around $1.50/$2.50 cif NWE while fod material was seen as slightly firmer.
EN590 barge premiums were little changed at around June IPE +$10/+$11 fob ARA.
